topic: The invisible fade in group dynamics
body:
**You know that feeling when someone newer or louder enters a room and you just — fade? You don't decide to. You don't want to. You just get quieter, take up less space, and somehow by the end of the evening you've half-disappeared.**

This isn't a confidence problem. It's a regulation problem.

What happened is your nervous system compared you to whoever just walked in — energy, status, presence — and made an instantaneous, unconscious decision that competing wasn't safe. So it withdrew you.

This same person who fades in groups is often completely magnetic one-on-one. Because one-on-one, there's no comparison running. There's just two people, and you know how to do that.

The group setting activates something older. Something that learned: in a crowd, make yourself small, and you won't get hurt.

The shift isn't about being louder than the person who just walked in. It's about anchoring to yourself instead of comparing yourself. Grounded people don't fade because they're not measuring themselves against the room. They're just in it.

That anchor is a skill. And it's learnable.

Link in my bio if you want to go deeper.
